Seasonality analysis of an index

Source: R/fct_seasonality.R
seasonality_analysis.Rd

Do some days of the week, weeks of the year, months or years of the US presidential cycle bring better returns than others? The returns of the complete periods (see seasonal_returns()) are summed up by group, and a Kruskal-Wallis test asks whether the differences between the groups are larger than chance would give. The test compares the ranks of the returns, so a few extreme months do not decide it, but it takes the returns as independent, which market returns are only roughly: calm and wild stretches come in runs.

Usage

seasonality_analysis(history, period = c("day", "week", "month", "year"))

Arguments

history

Price history of one index from get_history(), with all of it.

period

"day", "week", "month" or "year".

Value

NULL when the history has no complete period with one before it, or a list with:

index, period

What was analysed.

returns

The returns of seasonal_returns().

groups

A row per group that has returns, in their natural order: group, returns (how many), mean_pct, median_pct, up_pct (the share of the returns above 0), best_pct and worst_pct.

all

The same numbers for all the returns together, as a list.

p_value

The p-value of the Kruskal-Wallis test, NA when fewer than two groups have returns, or no group has two.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
spx <- get_history("S&P 500", as.Date("1950-01-01"))
analysis <- seasonality_analysis(spx, "month")
analysis$groups
analysis$p_value
seasonality_text(analysis)
}
